newsitem.title: GERMANY: German gypsies go to Euro-court on discrimination.
newsitem.headline: German gypsies go to Euro-court on discrimination.

text.p: German gypsies complained to the European Commission of Human Rights in Strasbourg on Thursday about a local court ruling which declared them unfit to sub-let apartments
A court in the western city of Bochum had ruled that gypsies were in general "not appropriate as sub-tenants of an apartment" because they were "a population group which largely has no fixed abode".

The chairman of the central council of German gypsies, Romani Rose, told a news conference it was important to have the "scandalous judgment" overturned, saying it was reminiscent of persecution of the gypsies under the Nazis.
The judge in the case used the German word "Zigeuner" for the gypsies, a term which the community find offensive, preferring to call themselves Sinti and Roma.
The president of the German judges' association, Rainer Voss, has criticised the use of the word "Zigeuner" and the conclusions which the Bochum judge drew.
Voss also said the judge regretted the language he had used in his judgment and the offence caused to Sinti and Roma.
The commission in Strasbourg screens cases to decide whether they should be passed on to the European Court of Human Rights.
